correctness.rationale: Generation in a finite nilpotent group decouples over Sylow subgroups, and Burnside's basis theorem reduces each Sylow component to spanning \(G_p/\Phi(G_p)\). A fixed pair can be extended to a generating \(d\)-set exactly when its rank is at least \(d_p-d+2\), giving the three local regimes \(d_p=d\), \(d_p=d-1\), and \(d_p\le d-2\). The quotient partner counts lift by \(|\Phi(G)|\). For divisibility, if \(g_p\notin\Phi_p\) then \(|\langle g_p\rangle\cap\Phi_p|=|g_p|/p\), while if \(g_p\in\Phi_p\) its full order is bounded by \(|\Phi_p|\); the displayed degree contains the required additional \(p\)-factor exactly in the former case. The packaged replay independently checks all elements of four mixed-prime groups and exhaustively checks a rank-three quotient profile.

originality.rationale: The primary 2020 source explicitly poses the degree-divisibility statement as Question 21. Its nilpotent Hamiltonicity proof gives a degree formula only for the full independence graph, and for p-groups this already covers the minimum-generator graph because all minimal generating sets have one size. For mixed-prime nilpotent groups the fixed-cardinality graph can be strictly smaller; the present formula resolves exactly that missing case. A later independence-property classification addresses a different pairwise property, and targeted statement-level searches did not locate the mixed-prime formula or an all-nilpotent resolution of Question 21.

value.rationale: The result answers an explicit published question on a broad structural class and gives more than divisibility: it determines every vertex degree in the minimum-generator layer. Finite nilpotent groups are a canonical testing ground for generation questions, and the formula exposes a natural Sylow-rank trichotomy that disappears in the full independence graph.
